scenarios.expected: Reference matches role limits, configured versus fixed concepts and actual file behavior.
scenarios.actual: Compared the permissions row with the app. The Administrator read the organization's configured contract types and opened a Confidential Contract created by the Legal Team Member, which is the row's reach. The account roles actually in use are administrator, business_user, contributor and legal_team_member, with no deployment-operator account role, so the operator row's "not an additional app account role" is accurate.

scenarios.expected: Reference matches role limits, configured versus fixed concepts and actual file behavior.
scenarios.actual: Checked the reference against the actual controls. Organization settings answered 403 "You do not have permission to perform this action." for this role while her own preference pane opened, which is the row's Administrator-only sentence. The Move to list showed each configured Status label beside its fixed Stage, including the seed's renamed "Signed, awaiting countersignature" against Signature. The key date form offers Date, Event and an optional Note with no assignee, while the task form offers Title, Assignee and an optional Due date, so Task due dates and Key dates are not equated. The Entities module lists our own Helix companies while the Contract overview carries separate "Our entity" and "Counterparties" fields. An actual Comparison was then computed and read on the seeded three-Version Word Document on C-21: "Compare with previous" on version 2 reached the ready state for the pair v1 → v2 and showed the counterparty's inserted wording, the chain still held v1, v2 and v3 afterwards, and reopening the same pair read it again without adding a Version. An SVG was offered as a plain download link with no reading panel while a PDF opened the panel and drew "Page 1 of 1"; a seeded Word document rendered as a converted PDF and Download returned the original .docx. A 105 MiB upload was refused with "over the 100 MB upload limit" and nothing was stored.

scenarios.expected: Reference matches role limits, configured versus fixed concepts and actual file behavior.
scenarios.actual: Read the reference as an operator would, signed out and with no app account: the formal reader opened /documentation/reference with all six sections, an On this page outline, the operator's own MAX_UPLOAD_MB fact, and the Deployment operator row of the permissions table reading "Maintains the installation and service configuration. This is an operational responsibility, not an additional app account role." Anonymous reading issued no app API calls, and the closing links reached "Configure a deployment" without a session. The row's claim about account roles was corroborated two ways, each labelled for what it is: the Administrator's actual role control offers only Administrator, Legal team member, Contributor and Business user, recorded as a browser walkthrough, and packages/db/src/schema/auth.ts declares the same four values in USER_ROLES, recorded as a source inspection. The earlier attempt listed the roles existing users happen to hold, which cannot establish the permitted set; that record is retained and superseded.
